activities.caption: pair each attention model with its bottleneck
activities.name: cogBottleneckMatch

config.prompt: Four models, four gates — pair each model with where it puts selection:

pairs.right: selection by physical properties, before semantic analysis
the unattended stream is turned down, not off — salient items break through
the bottleneck moved to response selection
perceptual selection depends on how loaded the current task is

config.why: Cherry's shadowing showed unattended speech leaves a physical trace but not meaning — early filtering — while hearing your own name in the ignored channel is what forced the attenuation revision; load theory reframed the question from where the gate sits to how much capacity the task consumes.

activities.anchor: multitasking means performing two attention-demanding tasks
activities.caption: true or false — the switching illusion
activities.name: cogSwitchJudge

statements.s: What feels like doing two things at once is rapid switching with switch costs, plus within-domain interference.
statements.why: Reading and spoken language compete for the same verbal resources — the dual-task logic this page runs on.

statements.s: Hands-free phone conversations leave braking reactions unimpaired, because the driver's hands stay on the wheel.
statements.why: Braking measurably slows — the bottleneck is attention, not the hands.

statements.s: Two tasks in the same domain interfere with each other far less than two tasks in different domains.
statements.why: The reverse: within-domain loads collide (driving and mental rotation); cross-domain pairs interfere far less.

statements.s: A phone conversation disrupts driving even when fully voice-controlled.
statements.why: Attention, not the hands, is the gate — the same reason you cannot fully process two streams at once.

activities.caption: file the evidence by working-memory component
activities.name: cogWmBuckets

config.prompt: File each piece of evidence under the part of the workspace it maps to:

items.label: the phonological similarity effect: B, C, D, T recalled worse than B, K, L, W
the word-length effect: recall falls with each added syllable
chess masters remember real positions brilliantly, random boards only slightly better than novices
about four chunks hold when rehearsal and grouping are controlled

config.why: The falsifiable dual-task logic that carved the workspace into components: concurrent speech disrupts verbal span, domains interfere far less across than within, and expertise extends the limit because capacity is counted in chunks, not pieces.

activities.caption: which curve is the serial, exhaustive scan?
activities.name: cogScanTrace

config.prompt: Memorise one to six digits; a probe appears; decide whether it was in the set. Which curve is the serial, exhaustive scan?

curves.label: a straight line, same tilt whether the probe was present or absent
a steeper line — absent probes cost extra per item
an almost flat line — every item compared at once

config.why: About 38 ms per item, with the same slope for present and absent probes: you compare against the whole set even after a match. A self-terminating scan would make absent trials cost more; a parallel process would flatten the line — subtracting constants from linear slopes is the template for mental-chronometry inference.

activities.anchor: Capacity is a budget spent in different currencies
activities.caption: call the controlled capacity estimate
activities.name: cogChunkEstimate

config.prompt: When rehearsal and grouping are controlled, how many chunks does the modern estimate give the workspace?
config.why: About 4 — the classic 7 ± 2 counted items while rehearsal ran free; the controlled estimate is roughly four chunks, and the chunk itself expands with expertise.
config.context: A chess master's 'item' is a whole pattern, not a piece.

config.prompt: The 1974 misinformation experiment, step by step — order the chain:
items: Participants watch footage of a collision
Speed estimates shift upward with the stronger verb
A week later, the 'smashed' group falsely remembers broken glass that was never there
config.why: One verb bent both the immediate estimate and the week-later memory — post-event misinformation alters testimony, which is why sequential line-ups and blind administration exist.

activities.anchor: a sincere witness can be sincerely wrong
activities.caption: find the faulty line — an eyewitness briefing
activities.name: cogWitnessSpot

config.prompt: One line of this eyewitness briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: Vividness and confidence are strong signs that a memory is accurate.
Recall rebuilds from fragments under schema control, so each retrieval rewrites the trace slightly.
Post-event misinformation can implant detailed, emotionally confident false memories.
Sequential line-ups and blind administration reduce false identifications.
config.correction: Confidence tracks coherence, not accuracy — vivid and certain does not mean correct; only confidence measured under pristine conditions at first identification tracks accuracy closely.
config.why: The Innocence Project's DNA exonerations — eyewitness misidentification involved in roughly 70% of cases — are this literature's institutional shadow.

activities.anchor: Human inference is not logic executed by flesh
activities.caption: drag the divider — same logic, two skins
activities.name: cogWasonCompare

config.prompt: The Wason selection task: the identical structure, two skins — drag the divider.

before.label: dressed as cards and vowels
before.text: The rule: if a card shows a vowel, its back is an even number. Fewer than a tenth of people pick the logically sufficient pair — the vowel and the odd number.

after.label: dressed as a social contract
after.text: If you take the benefit, you must pay the cost. Performance jumps to the 70–90% range for the identical logical structure — Cosmides and Tooby's cheater-detection reading.

config.why: The mind's inference machinery runs bare logic poorly but catches rule-breakers in exchanges of benefit and cost easily; the heuristics it defaults to (availability, representativeness, anchoring) are often ecologically rational rather than bugs.
